chunks: And Mūsā ibn Bakr narrated from Zurārah, who said: Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said:
If a man were to take a bundle of rods, or a branch containing rods, and strike him with it once, it would suffice for the number of lashes he intended to administer, according to the number of rods.

key_terms.أَجْزَأَهُ: it was sufficient and fulfilled the required count
key_terms.حُزْمَةً مِنْ قُضْبَانٍ: a bundle of rods used together as a striking implement
key_terms.عِدَّةِ الْقُضْبَانِ: the number of rods, which determines the counted lashes

ai.seo_question: Can one strike with a bundle of rods count as multiple lashes in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the manner of administering multiple lashes through a single strike using a bundle of rods. It indicates that one blow may count for multiple lashes when the implement contains a corresponding number of rods.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.5008 - Narrated by Musa ibn Bakr from Zurara who said:
Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said: "

If a man were to take a bundle of rods or a branch containing multiple rods and struck someone with it once, it would suffice him for however many lashes he intended to administer, equal to the number of rods in that bundle."
